name: What office construction costs are usually excluded from a tenant improvement allowance?

mainEntity.name: What costs are usually not covered by a tenant improvement allowance for an office in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What costs are usually not covered by a tenant improvement allowance for an office in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: A tenant improvement allowance rarely covers the full cost of an office build-out. In Los Angeles, allowances often pay for part of the hard construction work, but they may exclude design fees, structural engineering, permit and plan-check fees, furniture, IT and data cabling, audiovisual systems, moving expenses, and tenant-requested upgrades beyond the base scope. Some leases also exclude HVAC balancing, utility service changes, and after-hours work premiums. The exact exclusions matter more than the headline allowance amount. A tenant could receive a generous per-square-foot allowance and still face a large out-of-pocket bill if the space needs code upgrades or premium finishes. Before signing a lease, compare the allowance against the actual scope, confirm whether reimbursement is paid after completion or in draws, and verify what documents are required. In competitive markets like Beverly Hills or Westwood, lease language can make a major financial difference.
acceptedAnswer.description: A tenant improvement allowance often covers only a portion of hard construction costs. Architecture, engineering, permit fees, furniture, cabling, AV, moving costs, and some utility upgrades are commonly excluded. Landlords may also cap the allowance at a fixed amount per rentable square foot, so tenants still need cash for anything beyond the agreed scope.
